A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIRI research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and included appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture, UCI tabular, CIFAR-10, and CelebA experiments, including numerical results and imputed samples in Section 6 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds MAR/MNAR evaluations, downstream CIFAR-10 classification, and runtime measurements in Section 5 and Appendices H–I.

M1.justification: The MIRI updates, rectified-flow training loss, imputation ODE, initialization options, and Euler solver are retained. Appendix F extends the theoretical treatment to MAR and derives the same optimality condition, without introducing a different implemented procedure.

E1.justification: The underlying datasets are retained, but UCI evaluation expands from MCAR to MAR and MNAR missingness scenarios. CIFAR-10 evaluation also gains a downstream ten-class classification task beyond reconstruction and distributional fidelity.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Figure 4, v3 Figure 5 adds MIWAE, Sinkhorn, and TDM to the UCI comparisons while retaining the existing methods. The new runtime comparison also evaluates DiffPuter, previously only discussed, and includes the comparator labeled MOT in Table 6.

E3.justification: Existing dataset sizes and MCAR evaluations are retained. New protocols include MAR at reported 40%/80% missingness conditioned on a randomly selected half of the variables, MNAR at 20%/40%/60%, aggregate dataset rankings, classification accuracy, and timing 1000 samples across 50–5000 dimensions.

E4.justification: v3 adds robustness evaluations under MAR and MNAR and a dimensionality-dependent runtime analysis, including runtime failures and out-of-memory outcomes. These substantially extend v1's MCAR missing-rate analyses and retained image reconstruction examples.

E5.justification: The ten-run, mean±standard-deviation convention is retained. v3's checklist additionally identifies random masks/seeds as variability sources; this is a limited reporting clarification, without evidence of increased repetitions or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original toy-data and CIFAR fidelity tables retain their values, while v3 adds MAR/MNAR MMD results, aggregate rankings, classification accuracies, and runtimes. For example, Table 3 reports accuracy of 0.364 for MIRI versus 0.212 for HyperImpute at 60% missingness; Table 6 reports respective 5000-dimensional runtimes of 1.30 and 57.54 hours. v1's numerical UCI prose summaries are removed.

T1.justification: New Appendix F formulates a conditional-mutual-information objective under MAR and derives the same conditional-distribution optimality condition as Proposition 2. Appendix E also corrects the KL factorization in v1 Appendix D and explicitly derives its imputer-independent term. The original principal propositions and theorem remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introductory contributions retain the same central claims: mutual-information reduction, an optimal rectified-flow imputer, connections to existing methods, and strong tabular/image performance. The new conclusion summarizes these retained contributions.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and interpretation: it explicitly prioritizes distributional sampling over point prediction, explains the choice of rectified flow, acknowledges that the objective is not designed for MNAR, and interprets runtime scaling through vectorization. It retains the computational and population-level limitations and proposes a future time-series extension.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation URL, source information for additional baselines, and execution-time information. Hardware specifications remain unchanged, while v1's explicit recommendation of 100 Euler steps disappears. Detailed hyperparameters remain deferred outside the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for MIWAE, optimal-transport imputation, TDM, MMD, and McFlow, changes the introductory normalizing-flow attribution, and removes MisGAN. The central positioning relative to GAIN, round-robin methods, and conditional generative imputation remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 extensively edits the abstract, introduction, background, and experimental narrative. It restructures the contribution list, folds Practical Implementation into Section 3.4, moves the sequential-imputation appendix forward, and adds a separate conclusion and checklist. These are substantial editorial and structural changes beyond the added scientific material.

P2.justification: v3 adds ranking, classification, and runtime tables plus MAR/MNAR plots, and expands the MCAR chart with additional comparison series. It relocates the unchanged sequential-imputation schematic and combines the three existing appendix image grids into Figure 8 panels. The main result figures retain their original image content.

improvement.justification: v1's MCAR-only validation and qualitative computational-cost discussion gain MAR reasoning, MAR/MNAR comparisons, broader baselines, downstream classification, and measured scaling. Together these substantially strengthen evidence about applicability, practical utility, and computational cost. The explicit MNAR limitation also improves qualification of the results. Hyperparameter and classifier documentation remain incomplete in the PDFs, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and transparency.
